label: context.reference
text: Lifecycle handling uses the exact System interface system_lifecycle_events and never a hook engine, event bus, session lane, or ambient command runner. Its ordinary lifecycle.event vocabulary covers pre_tool_use, permission_request, post_tool_use, pre_compact, post_compact, session_start, session_end, user_prompt_submit, subagent_start, subagent_stop, stop, and interrupt. Session_end, subagent_start, and interrupt are reactive ordinary artifacts; other events may be sync or async only where lifecycle_contract.json declares a positive decision. A blocking continuation remains physically held while the provider run authors a derived checkpoint whose required_verified_artifacts uses artifact_label lifecycle.decision, mark lifecycle.decision.allowed, verifier lifecycle_decision, and params pinning the exact connection artifact/id, event id, emitter run, owner run, handler id, event, sync mode, handler type, and subject artifact. A denied, blocked, stopped, malformed, replayed, or mismatched decision produces VerificationFailed and no mark. Command handlers become granted Tool routes; MCP handlers become exact World-interface operation routes; Prompt handlers become exact provider input routes; Agent handlers become lifecycle.handler.task artifacts at an exact system_worker_* pin, and the destination provider normalizes its model output back to lifecycle.decision or lifecycle.handler.output. Async completion is a correlated lifecycle.handler.output movement with no control effect. Handler sources are a resolved lifecycle.connection snapshot with layer/path/trust and canonical destination-content SHA-256 evidence; enabled untrusted or modified handlers fail closed. Installation connects nothing: connection requires the exact artifact binding, provider run pin, formed grants, provider output/input checkpoints, handler destination/result checkpoints, and content-addressed run/policy evidence described by connection-authoring.schema.json. Additional context and replacement artifacts remain explicit refs in the admitted decision; their downstream use requires those refs to be authored on the exact continuation checkpoint and must not be inferred or auto-bound by runtime.
